name: Anterior spinothalamic tract
summary: Fibers carrying light touch and pressure that do not require fine localization end in the dorsal horn, cross in the anterior white commissure and ascend in the anterior funiculus as the anterior spinothalamic tract, merging with the lateral spinothalamic tract in the brainstem as the spinal lemniscus. Because crude touch travels both here and in the posterior columns, touch is rarely lost completely by a single cord lesion, which is why pain and temperature (single route) and vibration and position (single route) are the discriminating modalities in cord examination.

origin.note: Low-threshold mechanoreceptors; second-order cells in the nucleus proprius.

decussation.level: Anterior white commissure over several segments
decussation.note: Crosses less abruptly than the pain fibers.

waypoints.note: joins the spinal lemniscus and runs beside the medial lemniscus in the brainstem

termination: Ventral posterolateral nucleus of the thalamus and the somatosensory cortex.

lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Crude touch largely preserved on both sides because of the dual pathway
Loss of pain, temperature and crude touch below the level with preserved posterior column function

pearls: Test pain and vibration, not light touch, when localizing a cord lesion: touch has two routes and stays
The anterior spinothalamic tract is the reason 'sensory loss' after a cord lesion is rarely total
